items.text: Saudi forces say air defences destroyed two ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh, a cruise missile in the west and a drone near Jeddah overnight on 25–26 Nov, and blamed the [[p:Houthis]]; spokesman Turki al-Malki reported no civilian injuries. Earlier on 25 Nov the coalition said a projectile fell on Jeddah and Jazan port without casualties, and the Houthis claimed strikes on a Saudi refinery after the coalition hit Hodeidah.
items.notes: Interception claims are Saudi; refinery claim is Houthi. Explosion near midnight heard per AFP.

items.text: Iran's military claimed it shot down a US MQ-9 and other drones over the Strait of Hormuz on 25 Nov, said ships had hit mines there and told vessels to coordinate passage with it. US envoy [[p:Jared Kushner]] said [[p:Donald Trump]] keeps all options open on Iran and confirmed meetings with Tehran officials under [[p:JD Vance]]. Brent rose to about $94.7.
items.notes: Drone shoot-down and mine claims are Iranian, not confirmed by the US. Kushner remarks via The New Arab.

items.text: Medics said an Israeli airstrike in Deir al-Balah killed Gaza's deputy education minister Khaled Abu Nada and his wife; at least nine people were killed overnight, the third straight night of strikes despite the ceasefire. An Israeli official said [[p:Benjamin Netanyahu]] and [[p:Jared Kushner]] spoke on 24 Nov about Gaza's humanitarian situation after Kushner warned Israel risked becoming a pariah.
items.thread: Gaza ceasefire and Board of Peace plan
items.notes: Casualty figures from Gaza medics. Netanyahu–Kushner call per an anonymous Israeli official (Times of Israel liveblog).

items.text: EU leaders met in Brussels on 26 Nov on [[p:António Costa]]'s 2028–34 budget proposal (reported at €1.58tn; Euronews says almost €1.7tn) and a €45bn Commission loan for Ukraine financed by joint debt. Dutch PM [[p:Rob Jetten]] rejected the proposals and wants a smaller budget; Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Hungary want to opt out of the loan. A deal is targeted for 17–18 Dec.
items.notes: Budget totals differ between sources. Second source is AI-generated (PiQ). Summit outcome not yet known at logging.

items.country: United States / China / EU / Japan / India / Vietnam
items.text: The [[p:Office of the United States Trade Representative|USTR]] found 14 economies' 'structural excess capacity' actionable under [[e:Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974|Section 301]] and proposed tariff ceilings: 15% for the EU, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan, up to 18% for five Southeast Asian states and Bangladesh, 20% for China and Singapore, 25% for India and 35% for Vietnam. It made no finding on Mexico or Norway. A US official said the duties stay within existing deal caps and start January at the earliest; comments are due 5 Jan and hearings begin 25 Jan.
items.notes: Rates from the USTR proposal as summarised by Thompson Coburn; timing and 'no stacking' per an unnamed senior US official (AFP/Reuters via RTÉ). China's 20% comes on top of first-term tariffs.

items.text: USTR also proposed a 10% Section 301 tariff on finished Brazilian aircraft, ending the exemption confirmed in July; [[p:Jamieson Greer]] cited out-of-quota sugar and aircraft exports. Brazil's government said it would not yield to threats, called the tariffs illegal and did not rule out retaliation. [[p:Embraer]] {{note: Brazilian aircraft maker founded as a state company in 1969 in São José dos Campos.}} said it is studying the proposal; a hearing is set for 14 Jan.
items.notes: Brazilian government reaction from its statement as quoted by AIN.

items.text: Canada was left off the Section 301 list. [[p:Jamieson Greer]] told CNBC talks with Ottawa are stuck on steel, aluminium and autos, that any deal must accommodate Canada, and that [[p:Donald Trump]] and [[p:Mark Carney]] could meet several times before the December G20.
items.notes: Greer's statements; canonical URL on ctvnews.ca.

items.text: USTR made no Section 301 determination for Mexico, which still faces a 10% forced-labour Section 301 tariff on non-USMCA goods. [[p:Claudia Sheinbaum]] said on 19 Nov she hopes to close a steel, aluminium and auto tariff deal in December.
items.notes: Rio Times says it uses an automated newsroom; the no-determination fact is confirmed by Thompson Coburn and RTÉ.

items.text: The Commerce Department's [[p:Bureau of Industry and Security]] restricted remote access to advanced AI chips in non-US data centres by Chinese and other arms-embargoed companies, effective 19 Nov, with licences needed for data centres serving them large compute. It added licence requirements for most chip transfers to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, and formally rescinded most of the Biden-era AI Diffusion rule.
items.notes: Law-firm summaries of the BIS interim final rule; 90-day grace period for existing providers.

items.text: A federal jury in Brooklyn convicted [[p:Huawei]] {{note: Chinese telecoms company founded in Shenzhen in 1987 by Ren Zhengfei.}} on 10 of 12 counts, including bank fraud and theft of trade secrets, in the long-running case over its Iran business; it was acquitted of racketeering conspiracy. Huawei said it would take legal action.
items.notes: Verdict date 24 Nov per CNN URL; counts per Times of Israel liveblog and multiple outlets.

items.text: Republicans and Democrats are negotiating limits on [[e:2026 Iran war|Iran war]] operations in a funding deal before the 11 Dec deadline; Senate Armed Services chair [[p:Roger Wicker]] said Democrats can make their point without tying commanders' hands. House Democrats are split over risking a shutdown, and the Pentagon reportedly needs tens of billions more.
items.notes: Details read via a NewsCord summary of CNN, The Hill, NYT and WaPo reporting; underlying articles not read in full.
